questions.question: Who founded the Kanva dynasty after the death of the last Shunga ruler?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vasudeva**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Kanva dynasty was established by **Vasudeva**, who was a minister in the court of the last Shunga ruler, Devabhuti.
 
• Vasudeva is credited with overthrowing the Shunga dynasty and establishing the **Kanva rule around 73 BCE**.
 
• The Kanvas ruled from **73 BCE to 28 BCE** and were considered successors of the Shungas in the Magadha region.
 
• The Kanvas, like their predecessors, were **Brahmanical rulers** and continued to uphold Vedic traditions.
 
• The Kanva dynasty was ultimately defeated by the **Satavahanas**, marking the end of their rule.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Shunga Dynasty:**

 
 
• The Shunga dynasty preceded the Kanvas and was founded by **Pushyamitra Shunga** after the fall of the Mauryan Empire.
 
• It lasted from around **185 BCE to 73 BCE** and was marked by the revival of Brahmanical traditions.
 
 
 
• **Transition to Kanva Rule:**
 
 
• The last Shunga ruler, **Devabhuti**, was known for his weak leadership, leading to his assassination by Vasudeva.
 
• The Kanva dynasty emerged as a short-lived but significant successor to the Shungas.
 
 
 
• **Satavahana Dynasty:**
 
 
• The Satavahanas were a prominent South Indian dynasty that eventually overthrew the Kanvas.
 
• They are credited with re-establishing political stability in the Deccan region after the fall of the Kanvas.
 
 
 
• **Magadha:**
 
 
• Magadha served as the central region of power for successive dynasties, including the Mauryas, Shungas, and Kanvas.
 
• It remained a significant political and cultural hub in ancient India.

questions.question: Who among the following authorities acts as the Vice Chairman of the Concerned Zonal council on rotation basis for a period of one year?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chief Minister of the State**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Zonal Councils are statutory bodies established under the States Reorganization Act of 1956 to foster cooperation and coordination between states.
 
• Each Zonal Council is chaired by the Union Home Minister, while the Chief Minister of the state acts as the Vice Chairman on a rotational basis for one year.
 
• The rotation of Vice Chairmanship ensures equal representation of states within the concerned zone.
 
• There are five Zonal Councils in India: Northern, Central, Eastern, Western, and Southern, with each covering specific states and union territories.
 
• The Vice Chairman plays a key role in facilitating dialogue among member states to resolve inter-state issues and promote regional development.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Zonal Councils**

 
 
• These councils were created under Part III of the States Reorganization Act, 1956.
 
• The councils aim to resolve disputes, facilitate communication, and ensure balanced socio-economic development across states.
 
• They are advisory in nature and do not have legislative or executive powers.
 
 
 
• **Inter-State Council**
 
 
• It is a constitutional body established under Article 263 of the Indian Constitution.
 
• The council aims to investigate and discuss subjects of common interest between states and the center.
 
• Unlike Zonal Councils, it addresses broader issues affecting multiple states across India.
 
 
 
• **Union Home Minister's Role**
 
 
• The Union Home Minister serves as the Chairman of all Zonal Councils.
 
• As Chairman, the Home Minister ensures coordination between states and the central government.
 
 
 
• **States Reorganization Act, 1956**
 
 
• This act was responsible for the linguistic reorganization of states in India.
 
• It also led to the creation of Zonal Councils as a mechanism for fostering cooperation among states.

questions.question: When an object is moving with constant speed in a straight line, its acceleration:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**zero**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Acceleration is defined as the rate of change of velocity with respect to time.
 
• When an object is moving with constant speed in a straight line, its velocity remains unchanged over time.
 
• Since there is no change in velocity, the acceleration of the object is **zero**.
 
• Constant speed and straight-line motion imply no external force is causing a change in the object's velocity.
 
• This aligns with Newton's First Law of Motion, which states that an object will remain in uniform motion unless acted upon by an external force.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Velocity:** It is a vector quantity that describes the speed of an object in a specific direction.
 
• **Acceleration:** The rate at which an object’s velocity changes, calculated using the formula: *a = Δv / Δt*, where *Δv* is the change in velocity and *Δt* is the change in time.
 
• **Newton’s First Law:** An object at rest stays at rest, and an object in motion stays in motion at constant velocity unless acted upon by a net external force.
 
• **Uniform Motion:** When an object travels equal distances in equal intervals of time without changing its speed or direction.
 
• **Non-Uniform Motion:** When an object’s speed or direction changes, resulting in non-zero acceleration.

questions.question: Who was the founder of the Prarthana Samaj, which promoted social reform in Maharashtra?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Atmaram Pandurang**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Atmaram Pandurang was the **founder of the Prarthana Samaj**, established in 1867 in Bombay (now Mumbai).
 
• The Prarthana Samaj was inspired by the **Brahmo Samaj**, which advocated social and religious reform.
 
• It aimed to promote **social reforms**, such as the abolition of caste discrimination and child marriage, and encourage widow remarriage.
 
• Atmaram Pandurang was supported by prominent reformers like **Justice Mahadev Govind Ranade** and **R.G. Bhandarkar**.
 
• The organization emphasized **monotheism**, promoting a belief in one God while rejecting idol worship and rituals.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Prarthana Samaj:**

 
 
• The term "Prarthana" means prayer. The organization focused on **spiritual upliftment** and ethical teachings.
 
• It worked towards the **upliftment of women** and advocated for their education and rights.
 
• The Samaj was influenced by the **teachings of the Upanishads** and reformist ideas of the Brahmo Samaj.
 
 
 
• **Atmaram Pandurang:**
 
 
• He was a physician by profession and a leading social reformer in Maharashtra.
 
• He played a key role in initiating reform movements that addressed **superstitious beliefs** and social evils.
 
 
 
• **Justice Mahadev Govind Ranade:**
 
 
• Ranade was a prominent figure in the Prarthana Samaj and supported its reformist agenda.
 
• He emphasized the importance of education and economic development in social progress.
 
 
 
• **Brahmo Samaj:**
 
 
• Founded by Raja Ram Mohan Roy, it was a reformist movement that influenced the Prarthana Samaj.
 
• It advocated for **monotheism**, social reforms, and the rejection of caste discrimination.

questions.question: At which of the following places did 'Race Across India', Asia's longest-ever cycle race, culminate in March 2023?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kanyakumari**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• 'Race Across India,' Asia's longest-ever cycle race, culminated at **Kanyakumari** in March 2023.
 
• The race covered a total distance of approximately **3,655 kilometers**, starting from Srinagar, Jammu & Kashmir.
 
• It was officially recognized by the **World Ultra Cycling Association (WUCA)**.
 
• The event aimed to promote fitness, cycling culture, and awareness about sustainable transportation in India.
 
• The race spanned across multiple states, highlighting India's diverse geography and culture, and concluded at the southernmost tip of the Indian mainland, Kanyakumari.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kanyakumari** is the southernmost tip of mainland India and a popular tourist destination known for its beaches, Vivekananda Rock Memorial, and the confluence of three seas – the Arabian Sea, the Bay of Bengal, and the Indian Ocean.
 
• **World Ultra Cycling Association (WUCA)** is an international governing body that oversees ultra-distance cycling events, ensuring they meet global standards and provide recognition to athletes.
 
• The concept of ultra-distance cycling involves covering long distances, usually over hundreds or thousands of kilometers, and is a test of endurance and mental strength.
 
• Srinagar, the starting point of the race, is located in Jammu & Kashmir and is known for its scenic beauty, Dal Lake, and houseboats, making it an iconic location for such events.
 
• Events like 'Race Across India' are part of a larger global trend to encourage physical activity, reduce carbon footprints, and promote eco-friendly modes of transportation such as cycling.

questions.question: In an economy, the modernisation goal of a five-year plan is concerned with:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**New Technology**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Modernisation in a** five-year plan** refers to the adoption of **new technology** to improve productivity and efficiency across sectors in the economy.
 
• It involves replacing outdated or traditional technologies with advanced and innovative systems to meet global standards.
 
• This goal focuses on enhancing industrial output, agricultural practices, healthcare, and infrastructure through technological advancements.
 
• Modernisation is essential for achieving long-term economic growth and competitiveness in a globalised market.
 
• Examples include adopting renewable energy technologies, mechanised farming equipment, and digital transformation in governance and businesses.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Five-Year Plans:**

 
 
• The Five-Year Plans were centralised and integrated national economic programs in India, starting from 1951.
 
• These plans aimed at achieving various objectives, including growth, self-reliance, modernisation, and equity.
 
• The Planning Commission was responsible for formulating and overseeing these plans until its replacement by NITI Aayog in 2015.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Technology in Economic Growth:**
 
 
• Technological advancements help in reducing production costs and increasing output.
 
• They enable innovation, improve quality, and foster competitiveness in domestic and international markets.
 
• Examples include Artificial Intelligence (AI), Internet of Things (IoT), and biotechnology.
 
 
 
• **Modernisation and Agriculture:**
 
 
• Modernisation in agriculture involves the use of hybrid seeds, irrigation systems, and mechanised equipment.
 
• It helps in increasing yield, reducing dependency on manual labour, and ensuring food security.
 
 
 
• **Challenges of Modernisation:**
 
 
• High costs of adopting new technology may lead to inequality between developed and underdeveloped regions.
 
• It requires skilled manpower, which necessitates investment in education and training.
 
• Environmental concerns arise due to industrialisation and energy usage.

questions.question: As per the 2024 data published by Worldometer, which of the following neighbouring countries of India has the highest percentage of urban population?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Maldives**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• As per the 2024 data published by Worldometer, the **Maldives has the highest percentage of urban population** among India's neighboring countries.
 
• The Maldives is a small island nation with **100% urban population**, as all its inhabited islands are classified as urban areas.
 
• The country’s population is concentrated in urban centers like the capital city **Malé**, which accounts for a significant portion of the total population.
 
• The Maldives has a unique geographic structure with limited land, which influences its urbanization trends and high population density in urban areas.
 
• This contrasts with neighboring countries like Nepal, Bhutan, and Sri Lanka, which have predominantly rural populations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Urbanization:**

 
 
• Urbanization refers to the increasing proportion of a country's population living in urban areas.
 
• It often reflects economic development, industrialization, and modernization.
 
• Urban areas typically feature better access to infrastructure, education, and healthcare.
 
 
 
• **Geography of Maldives:**
 
 
• The Maldives is an archipelago consisting of 1,192 coral islands grouped into 26 atolls in the Indian Ocean.
 
• Its small land area and low elevation make it vulnerable to climate change and rising sea levels.
 
• All inhabited islands are urbanized due to the compact nature of settlements.
 
 
 
• **Urban Population in South Asia:**
 
 
• South Asia includes countries like India, Pakistan, Nepal, Bhutan, Sri Lanka, and the Maldives.
 
• Most South Asian countries have predominantly rural populations, except the Maldives.
 
• Urbanization rates vary significantly depending on economic development and geographic factors.
 
 
 
• **Worldometer:**
 
 
• Worldometer is a popular data platform that provides up-to-date statistics on demographics, population, and other global indicators.
 
• It is widely referenced for accurate and real-time global data.

questions.question: Which of the following Vedas mentions dance (Nrti) and danseuse (Nrtu)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rigveda**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Rigveda is considered the oldest among the four Vedas and is composed of hymns praising various deities.
 
• It mentions dance (Nrti) and danseuse (Nrtu) as part of its descriptions of cultural practices and rituals.
 
• Dance and music were integral aspects of Vedic rituals and cultural expressions during the Rigvedic period.
 
• The Rigveda primarily focuses on spiritual hymns but also provides insights into social and artistic practices.
 
• References to Nrti (dance) and Nrtu (danseuse) highlight the significance of performing arts in ancient Vedic society.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Vedas:**

 
 
• The Vedas are the most ancient religious texts of India and are considered the foundation of Hindu philosophy.
 
• There are four Vedas: Rigveda, Samaveda, Yajurveda, and Atharvaveda.
 
• Each Veda is divided into four parts: Samhitas (hymns), Brahmanas (rituals), Aranyakas (theology), and Upanishads (philosophy).
 
 
 
• **Rigveda:**
 
 
• The Rigveda consists of 1,028 hymns organized into ten books (mandalas).
 
• It is primarily composed in Sanskrit and is one of the oldest known texts in human history.
 
• The hymns are dedicated to various deities such as Agni (fire), Indra (rain and thunder), and Varuna (cosmic order).
 
 
 
• **Performing Arts in Vedic Era:**
 
 
• Dance, music, and drama were significant elements of Vedic rituals and ceremonies.
 
• Nrti (dance) and Nrtu (danseuse) symbolize the cultural and artistic expressions during the Rigvedic period.
 
• Music was often used in the chanting of Vedic hymns to invoke deities.
 
 
 
• **Samaveda and Music:**
 
 
• Although the Rigveda mentions dance, the Samaveda is more closely associated with music and chanting.
 
• The Samaveda focuses on melodies and chants that accompany rituals and ceremonies.

questions.question: Ishira and Maulik Shah jointly received the Sangeet Natak Akademi for the year 2018 for best performance in which dance genre?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kathak**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Ishira and Maulik Shah** are renowned performers and proponents of the Kathak dance form.
 
• The duo jointly received the **Sangeet Natak Akademi Award** in 2018, which is one of the highest national recognitions in performing arts.
 
• Kathak is a classical dance form from **North India**, known for its intricate footwork, swift spins, and expressive gestures.
 
• The award recognizes their dedication and contribution to preserving and promoting Kathak as an art form.
 
• The Sangeet Natak Akademi Award is presented by **India’s National Academy for Music, Dance, and Drama** to individuals for outstanding achievements in these fields.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kathak Dance**

 
 
• Kathak originates from the word “Katha,” meaning “story” in Sanskrit.
 
• It is traditionally performed by **storytellers called Kathakars** who narrate tales through dance and expressions.
 
• Kathak has three primary gharanas (styles): **Lucknow, Jaipur, and Banaras**, each with distinct techniques and emphasis.
 
• It incorporates elements of both Hindu and Muslim cultures, including temple dances and Mughal court performances.
 
• Its rhythmic patterns are often accompanied by **tabla and harmonium**, showcasing complex musical synchronization.
 
 
 
• **Sangeet Natak Akademi**
 
 
• Established in 1952, it is an autonomous body under the **Ministry of Culture, Government of India**.
 
• The Akademi promotes and preserves India’s performing arts, including music, dance, and drama.
 
• The **Sangeet Natak Akademi Award** is regarded as the highest recognition for performing artists in India.
 
• The award covers various forms of performing arts, including folk, tribal, and classical traditions.
 
 
 
• **Other Classical Dance Forms of India**
 
 
• India has **8 recognized classical dance forms**, including Bharatnatyam, Odissi, Kuchipudi, and Kathak.
 
• Each dance form represents the cultural heritage of its region and is steeped in traditions and spiritual significance.
 
• These dances are often performed during festivals, religious ceremonies, and cultural events.

questions.question: Who among the following was appointed as the Director General of Sashastra Seema Bal (SSB) in September 2024?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Amrit Mohan Prasad**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Amrit Mohan Prasad** was appointed as the **Director General of Sashastra Seema Bal (SSB)** in September 2024.
 
• Sashastra Seema Bal (SSB) is one of India's Central Armed Police Forces, primarily responsible for guarding India's borders with Nepal and Bhutan.
 
• Amrit Mohan Prasad is a senior Indian Police Service (IPS) officer with extensive experience in border security and internal policing.
 
• The Director General is the highest-ranking officer in the SSB and is responsible for operational command, administration, and strategic decision-making.
 
• This appointment aligns with the government’s focus on enhancing border security and ensuring effective management of the forces.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sashastra Seema Bal (SSB):**

 
 
• SSB was established in **1963** following the Sino-Indian War to strengthen India's border security.
 
• The force operates under the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) and is deployed along the borders of **Nepal and Bhutan**.
 
• The SSB's motto is **"Service, Security, and Brotherhood."**
 
 
 
• **Role of the Director General:**
 
 
• The DG oversees **policy formulation, operational readiness, and resource management** of the force.
 
• Key responsibilities include coordination with the Ministry of Home Affairs and ensuring inter-agency collaboration for border security.
 
 
 
• **Central Armed Police Forces (CAPFs):**
 
 
• India has seven CAPFs: CRPF, BSF, ITBP, CISF, SSB, NSG, and Assam Rifles.
 
• Each force has a specific mandate such as border security, internal security, or counter-insurgency operations.
 
 
 
• **India’s Border Security Strategy:**
 
 
• Focuses on deploying advanced technology like drones, surveillance systems, and intelligence-sharing mechanisms.
 
• Emphasizes coordination between CAPFs and the Indian Army for robust border management.

questions.question: Tamilisai Soundararajan was the Governor of which of the following states before resigning to contest the Lok Sabha elections in 2024?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Telangana**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Tamilisai Soundararajan** served as the Governor of Telangana from September 2019.
 
• She was appointed as the first woman Governor of Telangana after the state's formation in 2014.
 
• During her tenure, she also held additional charge as the Lieutenant Governor of Puducherry starting February 2021.
 
• Before her political career, Tamilisai Soundararajan was actively involved in medical practice and served as a gynecologist.
 
• She resigned from the governorship to contest the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, marking her return to active politics.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Role of a Governor:**

 
 
• The Governor is the constitutional head of a state in India, appointed by the President of India.
 
• The Governor's primary responsibility is to ensure that the state government functions within the framework of the Constitution.
 
• The Governor has powers such as giving assent to bills, summoning and dissolving the state legislature, and appointing the Chief Minister.
 
 
 
• **Telangana:**
 
 
• Telangana is the 29th state of India, officially formed on 2nd June 2014, after its separation from Andhra Pradesh.
 
• Its capital city is Hyderabad, which is also the shared capital with Andhra Pradesh for a period of 10 years.
 
• Telangana is known for its rich history, culture, and economic contributions, particularly in the IT and agriculture sectors.
 
 
 
• **2024 Lok Sabha Elections:**
 
 
• The Lok Sabha is the lower house of India's bicameral Parliament, and elections are held every five years to elect its members.
 
• The 2024 elections will decide the composition of the 18th Lok Sabha.
 
• It is expected to witness significant political activity, with leaders like Tamilisai Soundararajan contesting for seats.
 
 
 
• **Women in Governance:**
 
 
• Women have played significant roles in Indian politics, with leaders like Indira Gandhi, Sarojini Naidu, and others making impactful contributions.
 
• The appointment of women as Governors and Chief Ministers has been a step toward gender inclusivity in governance.
 
• As of 2023, there has been an increasing focus on promoting women’s participation in political and administrative roles.

questions.question: According to the National Multidimensional Poverty Index 2023, which state from the following has the highest percentage of poor people?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jharkhand**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• According to the National Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) 2023, **Jharkhand** recorded the highest percentage of poor people among all Indian states.
 
• The MPI measures poverty not only in terms of income but also based on multiple deprivations such as health, education, and living standards.
 
• **42.2% of Jharkhand's population** was identified as multidimensionally poor, reflecting significant challenges in access to basic services.
 
• States like Bihar and Uttar Pradesh followed Jharkhand closely in terms of high poverty percentages.
 
• The MPI 2023 is part of India's commitment to achieving the **Sustainable Development Goals (SDG)**, particularly Goal 1: No Poverty.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **National Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI):**

 
 
• The MPI is a comprehensive measure of poverty that goes beyond income levels and evaluates multiple factors such as health, education, and standard of living.
 
• It was developed by the **United Nations Development Programme (UNDP)** and Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative (OPHI).
 
• The index is aligned with India's commitment to the **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)**.
 
 
 
• **Key Indicators of MPI:**
 
 
• Health indicators include nutrition and child mortality.
 
• Education indicators evaluate years of schooling and school attendance.
 
• Living standards are assessed based on factors like access to electricity, drinking water, sanitation, housing, and cooking fuel.
 
 
 
• **India's MPI Progress:**
 
 
• India has made significant strides in reducing poverty, with **415 million people exiting multidimensional poverty** between 2005-06 and 2019-21.
 
• Despite these advances, some states like Jharkhand continue to face persistent challenges.
 
 
 
• **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs):**
 
 
• SDG 1 focuses on eradicating poverty in all its forms worldwide.

questions.question: Which of the following is a type of goods that a person can be excluded from enjoying its benefits?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Private Goods**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Private goods** are goods that are excludable, meaning individuals can be prevented from using them if they do not pay.
 
• Private goods are also **rivalrous**, as one person's consumption reduces the availability for others.
 
• Examples of private goods include food, clothing, cars, and housing.
 
• These goods are primarily provided through markets and are subject to the forces of supply and demand.
 
• Private goods contrast with public goods, which are non-excludable and non-rivalrous.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Public Goods**

 
 
• These are goods that are non-excludable (cannot prevent usage) and non-rivalrous (usage by one does not reduce availability to others).
 
• Examples include national defense, street lighting, and public parks.
 
• Public goods are often provided by governments due to market failure in supplying them adequately.
 
 
 
• **Merit Goods**
 
 
• These are goods that the government believes individuals undervalue and under-consume, such as education and healthcare.
 
• Merit goods are often subsidized or provided for free by the government.
 
 
 
• **Free Rider Problem**
 
 
• Occurs when individuals benefit from resources, goods, or services without paying for them.
 
• This is a common issue with public goods as people cannot be excluded from usage.
 
 
 
• **Excludability**
 
 
• A property of goods where access can be restricted to paying consumers.
 
• Private goods are excludable, while public goods are not.

questions.question: Large deposits of iron in the liver leads to a condition called __________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**hemosiderosis**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Hemosiderosis is a condition characterized by the abnormal accumulation of iron (hemosiderin) in the tissues, especially in organs like the liver, lungs, and spleen.
 
• It is generally caused by excessive iron intake, frequent blood transfusions, or conditions such as thalassemia and sickle cell anemia.
 
• The buildup of iron in the liver disrupts its normal function, leading to potential liver damage and conditions like cirrhosis.
 
• Hemosiderosis is distinct from hemochromatosis, as it is not always associated with tissue damage, although prolonged iron overload can lead to complications.
 
• Diagnosis typically involves blood tests, imaging studies, and sometimes a liver biopsy to confirm iron deposits.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hemosiderin:** A protein compound that stores iron in cells. Excessive hemosiderin can accumulate in tissues, leading to hemosiderosis.
 
• **Hemochromatosis:** A genetic disorder where the body absorbs too much iron from the diet, which can lead to organ damage.
 
• **Iron Overload Causes:** Common causes include repeated blood transfusions, excessive dietary iron, and certain hereditary conditions.
 
• **Symptoms of Iron Overload:** Fatigue, joint pain, abdominal pain, and in severe cases, organ dysfunction (e.g., liver or heart).
 
• **Treatment:** Management includes chelation therapy (removing excess iron) or phlebotomy (removing blood to reduce iron levels), depending on the underlying cause.

questions.question: The Dhrang Fair is a two-day festival in __________ and is celebrated in the honour of Saint Mekran Dada to pay homage and participate in religious rituals.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gujarat**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Dhrang Fair is celebrated annually in Gujarat in honour of Saint Mekran Dada.
 
• This fair is held in the village of Dhrang, which is located near Bhuj in the Kutch district of Gujarat.
 
• It is a two-day festival that includes religious rituals, cultural performances, and community gatherings.
 
• The fair attracts devotees and visitors who come to pay homage and participate in rituals associated with Saint Mekran Dada.
 
• Saint Mekran Dada is highly revered in Kutch for his spiritual contributions and teachings.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kutch District:**

 
 
• Kutch is the largest district in India by area and is located in the western state of Gujarat.
 
• It is known for its vibrant culture, handicrafts, and the famous Rann of Kutch salt marsh.
 
• The district hosts various fairs and festivals, including the Rann Utsav and Dhrang Fair.
 
 
 
• **Saint Mekran Dada:**
 
 
• Saint Mekran Dada was a spiritual leader and is remembered for his teachings of harmony and devotion.
 
• His shrine in Dhrang serves as a place of pilgrimage for devotees.
 
• The rituals performed during the fair commemorate his legacy and teachings.
 
 
 
• **Religious Fairs in Gujarat:**
 
 
• Gujarat hosts several religious fairs, such as the Tarnetar Fair, Bhavnath Mahadev Fair, and Vautha Mela.
 
• These fairs reflect the state's rich cultural heritage and diverse religious practices.
 
 
 
• **Cultural Significance:**
 
 
• The Dhrang Fair provides a platform to celebrate local traditions, music, and dance.
 
• It fosters a sense of community and preserves the region's cultural identity.

questions.question: What is the term used to describe the process by which water from oceans, lakes and rivers is converted into vapour and rises into the atmosphere?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Evaporation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Evaporation** is the process by which water changes from a liquid to a gaseous state, commonly referred to as water vapour.
 
• This process primarily occurs due to the **heat energy from the Sun**, which provides sufficient energy for water molecules to escape into the atmosphere.
 
• Evaporation is a crucial part of the **water cycle**, enabling the movement of water from Earth's surface to the atmosphere.
 
• It mainly takes place over large water bodies such as **oceans, lakes, and rivers**, but can also occur on moist surfaces like soil and plants.
 
• Factors like **temperature, wind speed, and humidity** significantly influence the rate of evaporation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Water Cycle:**

 
 
• The water cycle, also known as the **hydrological cycle**, describes the continuous movement of water within the Earth and atmosphere.
 
• Key processes include **evaporation**, **condensation**, **precipitation**, and **runoff**.
 
• This cycle is essential for maintaining Earth's water balance and supporting life.
 
 
 
• **Condensation:**
 
 
• Condensation is the process where water vapour in the atmosphere cools and changes back into liquid form.
 
• This process leads to the formation of **clouds**, fog, and dew.
 
 
 
• **Precipitation:**
 
 
• Precipitation occurs when condensed water vapour in clouds falls back to Earth due to gravity.
 
• Common forms include **rain, snow, sleet**, and hail.
 
 
 
• **Transpiration:**
 
 
• Transpiration is the release of water vapour from plants into the atmosphere through tiny pores called **stomata**.
 
• This process contributes to the overall amount of water vapour in the atmosphere.
